newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX HUB NATGAS ENDS UP ON AGAS, FIRM CASH.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX HUB NATGAS ENDS UP ON AGAS, FIRM CASH.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures pared morning gains but still ended higher Thursday in active trade, boosted by Wednesday's bullish weekly inventory data and stronger physical prices, industry sources said.

September closed up 9.3 cents at $2.444 per million British thermal units after surging this morning to a new high of $2.515. October, which also hit a new benchmark of $2.50 today, settled 9.6 cents higher at $2.452. Other deferreds ended up by 0.1 to 7.8 cents.

"It was a big day because of the AGAs, but volatility died down by mid-afternoon and prices fell back a little. I'm a little skeptical here, but some people are looking for $2.80 (basis Septemer)," said an East Coast trader, noting afternoon profit taking pressured prices off contract highs.
Wednesday's AGA report showing another low weekly stock build of 55 bcf triggered the latest move up, traders said.

While overall inventories are 133 bcf, or 7.5 percent, above last year's record lows, they still lag the 1994-1995 average by more than 400 bcf. Weekly Injections of 68 bcf through October are needed to get stocks back to 2.8 tcf.

Revised forecasts calling for warmer temperatures in parts of the East, Midwest and Texas by the weekend also should help support prices near-term, traders said. But the Southeast is expected to remain below-normal into next week.

With September breaking to new highs today, chart traders were hard pressed to peg resistance. After today's contract high of $2.515, which also coincides with $2.52, a spot continuation level from early February, next resistance was seen in the spot continuation gap between $2.64 and $2.89 from late January.

Minor support was pegged in the $2.34 area and then at $2.30, with better buying likely at $2.25-2.27. Further support points were at $2.20, $2.15-2.16 and then along the short-term up trendline at $2.14.

In the cash Wednesday, Gulf Coast prices jumped more than a dime to the mid-to-high $2.40s, while Midcon pipes were up a similar amount the low-$2.40s. New York city gate gas climbed into the low-$2.60s, up more than 10 cents on the day.
The NYMEX Henry Hub 12-month strip rose 4.3 cents to $2.352. NYMEX volume and open interest figures were unavailable today due to technical problems at the exchange.

On the KCBT, September finished 7.5 cents higher at $2.34, while deferreds ended up by 1.5 to eight cents. The East/West spread widened by 1.8 cents to 10.4 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 237 lots traded, down from Wednesday's total of 385.
